digest.component_or_area: review bot infrastructure / LLM provider seam
propositions: The production LLM-Review gate must be migrated from the direct Anthropic API to Bedrock inference profiles to close the dogfooding gap: clients predominantly reach Claude through Bedrock, so development against the direct API diverges from the production path users run.

The per-pass model split (frontier opus for Pass-1, standard sonnet for Pass-2/Pass-4 verify/coach, trivial haiku for utilities) is now established in code and must be preserved across the cutover by filling three independent class-slot environment variables rather than a single deprecated REBAR_LLM_MODEL knob.

The review-bot container image does not install the bedrock extra, so adding --extra bedrock to the Dockerfile's uv sync is a critical prerequisite that must be verified in-container BEFORE the model-class flip takes effect, else the first Bedrock call will hard-fail the gate that reviews every landing on main.

No cross-provider fallback is intentional: Bedrock throttling, mis-caching, or structured-output drift must surface to developers before clients encounter it, so a failure to invoke Bedrock must fail the gate closed rather than silently escalating to Anthropic.

The kill switch (deleting the three class slots and recreating the container) requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to remain present in the container so the Anthropic path has a credential, and the kill switch's end-to-end execution must be proven post-cutover to confirm the recovery lever has a working credential and not merely that config flipped.

A Bedrock InvokeModel client-error alarm monitoring AWS/Bedrock native metrics (rate of InvocationClientErrors / Invocations per inference profile) must exist and be proven to evaluate (state != INSUFFICIENT_DATA with real datapoints) BEFORE the cutover takes effect, as the existing VOTER_ERROR alarm cannot detect a partially degraded Bedrock that still votes.
